note: Shared expected values for focusOffset() / focus_offset() — the THIRD RSVP fixture,
src/renderer/src/lib/rsvp.embedded.test.ts. Never hand-write an expected offset in a
suite; add a case here so all three languages are pinned by the same numbers.
The contract under test is that a token is indexed and sliced in Unicode CODE POINTS,
not UTF-16 code units (backend/exporters/rsvp.py is the reference; both JS copies
normalize with Array.from). Widths therefore differ per character, so a code-unit
implementation measuring a surrogate HALF lands on a different offset instead of
measure(s) = sum over the CODE POINTS of s of (charWidths[cp] or defaultCharWidth).
Each suite builds that stub natively (Array.from / for c in s) — the stub is not the
thing under test, the implementation's own slicing is.
f: null means 'derive it with orpIndex(token)', which covers the composition of the
two functions end to end. A number is passed through verbatim (clamping included).
Fixture keys are deliberately camelCase in EVERY rsvp_*.json file — one shape read by
both a Python suite and two TS suites, so the Python side reads case["wordX"] and
root["defaultCharWidth"] rather than each language getting its own casing. Do NOT
'fix' these to snake_case: it breaks two suites.

cases.name: ASCII control
cases.why: 'the' -> f 1, so 10 px of prefix plus half of 'h': the same arithmetic the astral cases use

cases.name: astral focus char, ASCII on both sides
cases.why: 'a🎬b' -> f 1 is the EMOJI: 10 + 30/2 = 25. A code-unit impl slices token[1] = the lone HIGH surrogate (7) and gets 13.5

cases.name: astral prefix, ASCII focus
cases.why: '🎬clap' with f 1 measures the whole emoji as the prefix: 100 + 30 + 10/2 = 135. A code-unit impl measures the HIGH surrogate as the prefix and the LOW one as the focus -> 109.5

cases.name: astral prefix, astral focus, derived f
cases.why: '🎬clap' composed with orpIndex (5 code points -> 1): prefix 30 + 10/2 = 35. Pins the composition, not the divergence

cases.name: all-astral token
cases.why: '𝔘𝔫𝔦' -> f 1: prefix '𝔘' 24 + '𝔫' 26/2 = 37. A code-unit impl picks f 2 (the high surrogate of '𝔫') and gets 29

cases.name: astral in the SUFFIX only
cases.why: 'ab🎬cd' -> f 1: nothing past the focus glyph may affect the offset, so it is 'ab'-like (10 + 10/2 = 15). A code-unit impl picks f 2 and gets 23.5

cases.name: astral across a breakpoint, derived f
cases.why: '🚀…abcdef' is 13 code points -> f 3: prefix 3x34 = 102 + 34/2 = 119. A code-unit impl picks f 4 (a surrogate half) and gets 73

cases.name: out-of-range f clamps in code points
cases.why: '🎬' has ONE unit, so f 5 clamps to 0 and the whole emoji is centred: 30/2 = 15. A code-unit impl clamps to 1 and centres the LOW surrogate -> 9.5

cases.name: NFD single letter is measured composed
cases.why: 'e' + U+0301 normalises to one code point, so f 0 centres the composed 'é' (11): 11/2 = 5.5. Without the NFC pin f is 1, the prefix is 'e' (10) and the focus is the bare acute (3) -> 11.5

cases.name: NFD mark inside the token shifts the measured prefix
cases.why: 'n' + U+0303 + 'o' composes to 2 code points, so f 1 measures the prefix 'ñ' (13) and centres 'o' (10): 18. Un-normalised, the prefix is 'n' (10) and the focus is the tilde (4) -> 12

cases.name: RESIDUAL: mark with no precomposed form is measured as its own glyph
cases.why: ACCEPTED DELTA: U+0348 cannot compose, so f 1 measures the prefix 'a' (10) and centres the mark (6) -> 13, with or without normalisation. Pinned so the residual is a known number rather than a surprise

cases.name: unpaired surrogate is measured whole, as one unit
cases.why: MALFORMED but documented: 'a\ud83cb' -> f 1 measures the lone surrogate itself (7), so 10 + 3.5 = 13.5. Both indexings agree here — the point is that it can never be split or dropped
